instructions: In a bowl, mash together the feta, kefalotyri, egg, parsley, dill and pepper until creamy. No salt is needed.
Work in the flour and 3/4 cup of the breadcrumbs until the mixture is thick enough to roll. Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the mixture into walnut-sized balls. Roll each ball in the remaining 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, set them on a plate and chill for 10 minutes.
Pour the oil into a heavy pot, about 1 inch deep, and heat over medium to 350°F. No thermometer? A breadcrumb dropped in should sizzle right away.
Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden and crisp. Don't crowd the pot.
Transfer the croquettes to a plate lined with paper towels. Serve warm with a drizzle of honey.
To make them ahead, freeze the breaded balls before frying. Fry them straight from frozen, adding about 1 minute.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings, so this follows Maria's Cook Book (no rating shown): feta and kefalotyri bound with egg, flour and breadcrumbs, chilled, breaded and fried, halved to serve four. The Family Cooking and Lemon & Olives show the same shape with kasseri or gouda, and Gourmet Traveller's is a larger, spicier batch. Feta and kefalotyri often use animal rennet, so choose ones labelled vegetarian.
